questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Other endings are studied according to the _____ on board other than kings, e.g. rook and pawn versus rook endgame.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “board”. It names more than one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Endgame” part of the Chess article.

questions.proof: The endgame is the part of the game when there are few pieces left on the board.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The _____ whose king is in check must make a move that escapes the check.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “whose”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Check and checkmate” part of the Chess article.

questions.proof: The options when a player is in check are moving the king, capturing the threatening piece, or moving another piece between the threatening piece and the king.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “For _____, king and pawn endgames have only kings and pawns on one or both sides, and the task of the stronger side is to promote one of the pawns.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “king”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Endgame” part of the Chess article.

questions.proof: For example, king and pawn endgames have only kings and pawns on one or both sides, and the task of the stronger side is to promote one of the pawns.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Chess engines are _____ systems that can play chess games against human opponents.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “systems”. It names one thing, not an action.
